title: Flux admin operator: playlet index and runtime mapper
creator: Alexandra Chen
description: Build a lightweight index and runtime mapping service for admin playlets (small runnable runbook snippets) so support flows can be quickly resolved by automated and human operators. The Flux operator will provide a discoverable registry, metadata-driven routing (safety tier, required permissions, estimated token cost), and a runtime mapper that picks the best execution environment (hosted, dedicated, private) based on policy. This ticket implements backend indexing, a small API for lookups, and integration points for the Console and operator CLI.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Playlet Index service that stores immutable playlet records (id, version, tags, safety-level, estimated-cost, inputs schema, telemetry hooks). Add a Runtime Mapper component that evaluates policy rules (latency SLO, customer tier, geographic constraints) and returns execution bindings (model variant, cluster pool, quantization profile). Expose a /v1/playlets/{id}/resolve endpoint and a query API for fuzzy discovery. Use existing KV-store (config-service) for records and the routing policy evaluator from Smart Routing infra. Instrument heavy hits for caching and add audit logging for every resolve call.
acceptance_criteria: Playlet Index API supports create/read/list with version pinning and tag filters
Runtime Mapper returns deterministic bindings for a set of test policies (unit tests)
Resolve calls produce structured audit logs compatible with the Console logs pipeline
End-to-end demo: Console playlet picker resolves a playlet and invokes it on the mapped runtime
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for playlet artefact encryption

2026-03-08 - Decided to reuse Smart Routing policy engine for runtime mapping to reduce duplication; will add a small adapter layer
2026-03-10 - Initial schema for playlet metadata committed in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playlets/tree/main/schema

risks: Playlet execution bindings may surface incompatible model variants leading to silent failures; mitigated by compatibility matrix and fast-canary fallback
High cardinality queries on playlet tags could increase latency; plan to add TTL-based caches and index shards
Audit log volume increase; need to verify Console retention and cost impact before wide rollout
